gpu.compute.bf16.note: 10 cores x 128 ALUs x 2 FLOP x ~1.58 GHz. No tensor cores on M4. Measured 2026-10-04 with benchmarks/compute.py: FMA-chain kernel, best of 20 (fp16 3.71). mx.matmul bf16 reaches 3.01-3.13 (n = 1024-8192). Short runs: burst, not sustained.

core.capacity.note: Per-core on-chip SRAM: registers, threadgroup memory and cache. Since M3 (Dynamic Caching) these share one memory per core; Apple does not publish its size. benchmarks/hierarchy.py (2026-10-06): with one threadgroup per core, buffers up to 128-176 KiB are served at ~1.35 TB/s; with four groups per core the visible cache drops below 48 KiB, i.e. registers take the same SRAM. 512 KiB is a deliberate upper estimate (about 2x the largest observed cache), not a measurement.

core.bandwidth.note: Aggregate bandwidth from the shared on-chip cache (GPU L2) into the cores. benchmarks/hierarchy.py shared-read sweep, 160 groups, every group streams the whole buffer: 700-774 GB/s (best) for 0.4-2.9 MiB, falling from 4 MiB (SLC, 480 -> 150 GB/s) to DRAM speed by ~16 MiB. Burst, load avg ~4. Threadgroup memory reads reach 690-890 GB/s aggregate (not a boundary in this model).

chip.capacity.note: Bytes of on-chip storage the GPU sees between DRAM and its cores (GPU L2 plus system level cache), the M of the red-blue pebble bound. Unpublished; the estimate is the commonly reported 8 MB SLC. Measured 2026-10-04 with benchmarks/bandwidth.py --sweep-per-octave 4: reads stay at ~230 GB/s up to 2.4 MiB, fall gradually, and reach DRAM speed (~95 GB/s) at 11.3 MiB. `measured` takes the upper edge, rounded up to 12 MiB: a larger assumed M weakens the lower bound. The chosen upper edge is not a certified upper bound on physical capacity, so validity is conditional.

chip.bandwidth.note: GPU-alone achievable bandwidth; upper-bounded by total_bandwidth. Measured 2026-10-03 with benchmarks/bandwidth.py, 1 GiB buffer, best of 20 (median 102.2). Write 94.9, copy 95.0 GB/s. Reads of 1-2 MiB reach ~250 GB/s; from 8 MiB up it is DRAM speed.

assumptions: Fixed explicit KV representation; rates/capacities are calibration assumptions.
An operator lower bound is not an attainable schedule or an upper bound.
Experimental fused proof is excluded unless explicitly requested.
